question: A man bought 4 books for ₹50 each, 5 books for ₹60 each and 6 books for ₹70 each. The average cost of a book for the man is (round up to two decimal places):
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly calculate the **Weighted Average** of the books.

Total items = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 books.

Weighted Sum = (4 × 50) + (5 × 60) + (6 × 70) = 200 + 300 + 420 = ₹920.

Average Cost = 920 ÷ 15 = ₹61.333...

**∴ The correct answer is ₹61.33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of books (n₁) = 4, Price (p₁) = ₹50

Number of books (n₂) = 5, Price (p₂) = ₹60

Number of books (n₃) = 6, Price (p₃) = ₹70

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Total Value) ÷ (Total Number of Units)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dbe2be7b3a5102d6a05cab89e8e0a58cf8ff34c83f8acd9400f50cb71e3e87d.png] 

⇒ **Total Cost** = (4 × 50) + (5 × 60) + (6 × 70)

⇒ **Total Cost** = 200 + 300 + 420 = ₹920

⇒ **Total Books** = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15

⇒ **Average Cost** = 920 ÷ 15

⇒ **Average Cost** = 61.3333...

**∴ The correct answer is ₹61.33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

It is calculated as Σ(nᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σnᵢ, where n is the frequency and x is the value.

Rounding Decimals

When rounding to two decimal places, check the third decimal; if it is 5 or more, round up the second digit.

Properties of Average

The average always lies between the minimum and maximum values of the data set (50 < 61.33 < 70).
